correctness.rationale: The undeleted 17-vertex graph is non-word-representable by Petyuk's published Theorem 5 proof. For each vertex deletion, an explicit 16-vertex total order is supplied. Reorienting every overlap edge forward in that order is acyclic by construction, and exhaustive path replay finds no shortcut. By the standard semi-transitive characterization, all 17 deletions are word-representable. Every proper induced subgraph lies inside one of these deletions, so hereditary closure proves the full criticality claim.

value.rationale: The originating paper explicitly asks whether its 17-vertex obstruction is minimum inside S(3,3). Proving the displayed obstruction is itself induced-subgraph-minimal is a natural structural first step: it rules out every attempt to shorten the existing proof by simply deleting vertices and shows that any smaller ambient obstruction must use a genuinely different vertex set. The result is a complete finite boundary statement with explicit positive certificates rather than a routine recount.
